rationale: Round 0 built, ran correctly, and hit no ICE, so the constraints allow pushing obfuscation strength up from the conservative baseline. lpbench is a tiny (5064-byte text), compute-bound numeric benchmark whose hot functions (dgefa, dgesl, daxpy, matgen) are tight arithmetic loops, so I favor low-overhead transformations: SUB gets the highest weight since instruction substitution is cheap, composable, and directly obscures the floating-point and integer idioms of the LINPACK/FFT kernels; SPLIT and IGV follow (IGV especially for diversity, since global variable encoding reliably breaks pattern recognition in small binaries) while keeping their modest runtime/size cost weights low so they fire broadly. IBR and ICALL are kept at strong security weights with moderate cost sensitivity — indirect branching and calls frustrate static control-flow recovery and are affordable even in hot loops given the small code size. BCF and FLA are deliberately restrained (high RuntimeCost/SizeCost weights): bogus control flow and flattening multiply loop-body work in daxpy/dgefa where nearly all runtime is spent, and the 5 KB text budget leaves little headroom, so these passes should apply only where per-function cost features justify them rather than program-wide. CorrectnessRisk weights stay elevated for BCF/FLA to preserve the clean round-0 correctness result.
